chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Mufaddal ibn 'Umar said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "It is not fitting for the believer to humble himself." I asked: "How does he humble himself?" He said: "He enters into that which he makes excuse for (i.e., minor faults or things he considers beneath his dignity)."

key_terms.يَعْتَذِرُ: to make excuse or feel unworthy

ai.seo_question: What does it mean for a believer to humble himself according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines self-humiliation not as physical prostration, but as accepting roles or duties for which one lacks the requisite competence or dignity, thereby creating a valid excuse for failure. This concept underscores the Shia emphasis on *karamah* (nobility) and the responsibility of the believer to maintain spiritual and social integrity by avoiding positions of authority or engagement where they are likely to falter. It serves as a practical guideline for evaluating one's capacity before committing to religious or social obligations.
